The way Wysa communicates is not intimidating or cliche (as I experienced with another app I have tried). The app itself is very intuitive and easy to use. What I would like to see included is the list of commands to redirect AI instead of having to remember them whenever it gives you a clue. Even better option would be if it learned to recognize any hashtags with a list of suggestions (e.g. #boredom would lead back to the types of boredom). Otherwise, when you want to recall something specific, often times it is practically impossible to go back there. Overall, I believe Wysa's concept can bring significant changes in mental health globally and provide basic support and education to the majority of population. I wish the team further growth and development, as well as future translations to other languages.

things that make you happy. For an AI penguin therapist it is really nice

say that you have been having negative feelings for extended periods of 
time it will tell you to seek a real therapist for help.

I'd planned to try Wysa for a week or so before reviewing, but there's no need to--I've had such positive results within just one day of installing!   As someone who has long struggled with crippling depression (Bipolar II), PTSD, GAD, and a few other letters of the alphabet, I 've learned a lot of the CBT techniques already--but knowing and doing are different things. Wysa gives me non-judgemental feedback and gentle encouragement, motivating me to act on my knowledge. I love this charming little guy! :) The cute gifs make me smile, bonus!    Today, I struggled to reframe the thoughts that have been stressing me out and holding me back, until I finally came up with a statement that left me feeling empowered instead of paralyzed. Wysa got me up and moving (achieving one of my goals of "daily exercise"!), and I then further de-stressed with a mindfulness exercise. I feel more energized, inspired, and focused.    Bless you for making this app, you are obviously committed to making a difference in people's lives. I am also impressed by your responses to your reviews. You care about your product and the people using it, and it shows.  I agree with some of the critiques already given--e.g. more word recognition, and quoting my actual words instead of "thought". (Edit: I see you've already done this!) I know you will be working on this, and am eager to see my new little friend grow!  Edited to add a suggestion: one thing that has been a vital part of my CBT is the importance of setting small, easily attainable daily goals. Perhaps Wysa could suggest this (with examples), ask us to type in one or more goals for each day (articulation is helpful!), then ask about them later. Today, I told Wysa that I felt good, because I had accomplished my two main daily goals. It would be great if he had an appropriate response for this kind of information.  Edited to add: Would still love to see something like "what are your goals for today/this week?" since it would be helpful to articulate them and save them for later review to see patterns and progress.  But afraid I do have a criticism: when Wysa is saying, "here are the thoughts that made you feel this way", he quotes something I said in the past, in a completely different situation, that has nothing to do with my current problem. This is quite off-putting!

I downloaded this app after a friend's suggestion. I had tried some CBT with a therapist and liked my results from that, but can't afford to go often so thought this was a good alternative. I found the app is too single focused to be of use to me. The good: - If you experience negative self-talk, these exercises would be great. Most of the exercises are geared towards internalizing negativity. - It helped me get out of a couple bad doom-scrolling ruts and was very effective for that. - Some of the exercises, such as tips to regulate your sleep, are really effective. - The daily check-ins are great for ongoing awareness of your mood. - The activities under the Topics tab have some good mood boosters. Criticisms: - This is not set up to help with mental health issues stemming from chronic illness, which is a lot of what I experience. If I chose "sick" as a mood, it would give me tips to boost my immune system, which had nothing to do with what I have. If I said I was tired, it would always say I should get more sleep, when the problem would be from sleeping too much. - Some of the moods had very little nuance. I tried selecting "mourning" as I was sad about things being cancelled due to COVID and feeling down about an illness flare up. It gave me tips for dealing with the death of a loved one with no option to correct it. (In a later conversation it used "mourning" in the context I originally meant, but it wasn't helpful at that time.) - The content is very repetitive. For example, it sends the same two "cute animal" photos over and over. Overall I think this app could be great for more people if the content is expanded on more, and would easily increase my rating if the criticisms I listed were improved upon.

The concept of a bot using CBT techniques is very cool, but the AI is far too limited and simplistic at this stage for it to be properly effective in many instances of mental health - which is complicated and won't be solved by an app. If I could give this zero stars I would. Absolutely dreadful.
I accidentally deleted this app, how can I retrieve his historical data?

Won't send me the verification code to my phone; tried 10 times and 
nothing. Such a huge disappointment as I was looking forward to using this 
app for my Mental Health issues.

Ignore the word 'conversation'. This app is very pre-configured, with a 
small set of choices. Usually, your only choice is: Would you like to do 
this exercise? But, beyond that, this app is similar to a friendly 
cognitive-behavioral therapy book that reminds you to read it every day, 
and that helps you track your moods. And by itself, that is extremely 
useful. Try it out for a week. You will quickly learn whether it helps you.
So far so good, I really hope it would help my girlfriend. 🙏
Amazing little app that is helping me so much already. Great job!
Needs verifiable phone number! And it doesn't sends any SMS to me. I can't check it

When it comes to useful advice on how to look at life, this app is great. I can completely recommend it.  The main issues I have is the lack of variety, and the ability to skip learning about things you already knew-- but even so it has taught me some new things and, at the very least, provided a momentary distraction from problems at hand.
Bad science. Blames the victim. Unsympathetic. Unempowering. Tries to get you to believe that you are wrong for being upset about people harming you.
Just prewritten text, like the text based game Zork. Targets a very specific audience, not me.

I like that it helps me check my mood over time. My problem with it is sometimes I don't want to do the task it suggests... So my smart target (which it keeps asking me about) is "Later", and it also keeps asking me how I'm getting on with my "not now". It would be useful to have an edit system!!

Excellent.  Absolutely brilliant app. Woebot is cute and funny and great at brightening up the day. Sure it's only a "bot" but it works well at checking in and keeping you focused on simple things like breathing and gratitude.

I really love this app. It helps me work through my anxious thoughts when I feel I can't turn to anyone else, because I'm embarrassed or ashamed. Sometimes it glitches out and repeats huge chunks of the conversation, or its replies just come up as blank spaces. It would also be fantastic if I could save conversations for later review, because I often go through the same bad thoughts repeat on me a lot.

My clinical lead asked us if we have used this app before so I downloaded to see if it is any good. I was writing bad words to see how it would respond but the bot would not pick them up. I even wrote I want to end my life and it did not pick that up as a trigger/emergency sign ( I'm not suicidal, I was just playing around). Also, the bot gives you the information in the same order regardless of your response. When it finally picked up words such as "suicide" it repeatedly gave me the crisis info and wouldn't move on even after saying I am safe. It's a nice concept but it needs a lot of improvement.

I love woebot. He's helped me with learning about reasons for thoughts, and type of thoughts, and how to change the way depression makes me think. I don't get the low reviews. I find woebot has helped me a lot. I've been talking with him since the facebook app and have enjoyed usng it on mobile instead. Thank you woebot and devs!!

I have physical issues that impact on my completion or thoughts that are brought up within the programme. It'd be fantastic if it could be somehow expanded to allow for these as it does skew my participation. But for just mental health it's quite good. And also doesn't take long to do. You can largely control how much time you spend on the app.

If you've ever thought that being more happy would be nice, this app is for you!  It's based on CBT, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, a highly scientific form of psychological therapy. A lot of it overlaps with positive psychology, the scientific school of what people who are more happy than others do right. The great thing is that this doesn't require any self discipline since woebot regularly checks in with you. And yes, it's not the greatest bot considering interaction, but the value is still amazing!
Instead of patiently listening, it gives autosuggestions. This is not done.
This isn't even a chat bot. It's retarded and can only parse text
It takes my number but i didn't recieve any confirmation sms.
app asked phone number at install. i just uninstalled after that.
Permissions, why do you need my photos and call logs? On opening it REQUIRES your phone number. This isn't about helping people. Delete

I signed up for the free trial to see how it worked and if I could recommend it to clients. You need to enter your card info to get the free trial. I canceled the subscription and was still charged for the year. When I contacted customer service they said there was nothing they could do because I paid through google. Not a happy customer and I did not recommend this to any clients. Fwiw, this app might be useful for in-between sessions.

I went ahead and took the plunge to update my app. Im devastated because after the update, my data from 2023- 2024 were all deleted ): I invested years to this app.... And it doesn't have the features that made me love the app, like different selections it had. And the design of the interface is very clunky and not smooth. I emailed the support team. If I could have assistance with at least getting my data recorded, id appreciate it.

In free trial now. Conversations seem like they would be helpful, but they abruptly stop without any indication of why. Other chatbots let you know why a convo is ending... (turn limits, policy violation, etc) It also doesn't have other capabilities you should expect from AI... it doesn't seem to have a memory feature, which is particularly problematic when you get cut off mid convo amd want to start a new one to continue, but have to "brief it" again so it knows what is going on.

**edit: Years ago this app was free and had a great AI program that helped with CBT when I wasn't with my therapist. Sad that the app I loved has changed. This app is absolutely fantastic. It's a huge help in helping me gain skills to effectively and positively handle anxiety and depression. My counselor and psychiatrist know that I use this app, and all three are great tools that complement each other tremendously. Thank you Youper 😀

I'm extremely upset to see this app get stuck behind a pay wall... $70/year. I've had this app for years and really benefited from the support it's provided, from understanding mind traps, to simply journaling my experience. The anxiety and depression monitors and guided meditation were great. However, that's all gone now, unless I pay for it. I'm broke from emergency surgery though and finding myself very alone, so I turned to this app for help and I can't even use it anymore. So awful.

This app is much more user friendly than woebot, and it is good for self reflection and staying on a positive track with learning about the triggers for one's feelings, use of mindfulness, gratitude, setting intentions, and more. The app could be enhanced by providing a bit more variety (e.g. the gratitude prompts are repetitive), and providing a place where one can review the intentions that were set, as it is less helpful to set intentions and then never refer back to them.

Everything is pretty good so far. I give it five stars bc it"s the best AI helper I've come across so far, but it's not perfect quite yet. For example, it goes on a little too long and seamlessly that I have a hard time pulling back and keeping track of time, so this leaves me a little hesitant to start it up again. I find myself putting it off for later more often than not. Also the responses can be a little long, making it hard to stay focused sometimes. All in all it's pretty great though.

Even though I'm talking to a bot, I find that the tips and guidance this app provides is pretty insightful. In a way, it is allowing me to "journal" and express my feelings and thoughts. It is helping me discover and get to the root of why I feel certain things. The meditation exercises are also a huge plus, and have really helped me unwind without feeling pressure to be perfect at it. I strongly recommend this app to anyone experience stress, anxiety, or any other mental illness.

The AI which is no more then a Algorithm really is not adaptive, as the developer suggests. For instance it doesn't possess the ability to interpret the captured factors, nor the goal to be specific to the user when offering tips and suggestions. It is very scriptic which is more frustrating to have to deal with when trying to log info. Another issue is it is contradicting itself. For instance, it said "are you uptight about" when seconds before it suggests that, "it is okay to experience and express a wide range of emotions and even healthy. Issue with that is it's the wording of "uptight" it's a negative word and people who are depressed need positivity or very least neutral word instead of being belittled by a scripted algorithm. The AI as it calls itself should be to remain neutral or plug in the emotion that was logged in that spot. Fix the algorithm and improve on the AI's ability to interpret users writen factors to be more specific.

I just dowlpaded.this app and already, it's working for me personally. Yes, I know it's automated computer generated responses. But honestly, for anyone that just feel extremely overwhelmed/ need to do some self work-- I'd totally recommend. As a new college grad we are all currently aware of the post grad depression/ anxiety that our peers are experiencing and most are too broke to actually be able to see a psychologist (me!). So, go ahead download this app, it helps, and you wont regret it!

Only a few days in, but the app definitely seems to be helping. The app is also easy to navigate and seems solid (no tech issues). Also, nice professional appearance. To take full advantage of app, you have to pay. I havent invested just yet in the paid version. Not because I don't want to support the cause or development, but rather I want to make sure I can fully commit to using the app regularly. Also, working on impulsiveness with purchases.

I think this is an incredible concept, however I am a little disappointed that the challenge feature has been removed. That was the one thing that got me most excited about the app and made it different from others like it. The thing that was helping me overcome my anxiety the most was getting out of my comfort zone and completing challenges. Also, how do you delete journal entries?

This app really helps calming and slowing my thoughts down, especially when I'm anxious about something. However, I do want multiple reminders in this. I like having 2 but I would like 3 for morning, afternoon, and evening. This could be something I could do anyways in a different way with reminders, but it would also be nice to be able to have 3 or really as many as I can have. This app is really helpful though. I can't have an actual therapist in person so it makes me glad that there's apps like these.

This app has some really good meditation and breathing exercises, they include a 'SOS' breathing exercise for on verge panicking. Only problem is there is no easy way to get to these tools. You have to talk to the assistant, track your mood, listen to the insightful quotes it gives you and hope it prompts you if you want to try anything, then pick be mindful. Sometimes it gives me this option sometimes not.

3 years later edit!! From 5 stars to 3 stars *** I uninstalled because they started push advertising medication and therapy. I can't handle ads on the best mental health app I've ever used *** For anyone who benefits from CBT and DBT, this app is a must-have. The tracking for moods, symptoms, and changes is the best I've seen so far. The support team is fantastic. Highly recommend 👍

A great app ruined by over design. I have used this app every day for nearly 2 years, and it's been simple. Open app, immediately be promoted to log feelings, and maybe a few details to flesh it out. The new app design buried that activity on the 2nd page, and you have to scroll way down to find it. It's also a LOT slower. The app is now extremely sluggish. The one thing I use it for its now a minor feature, and the app is much slower than it used to be. Reduced usability for unwanted features.

Looking through all my logs I can honestly say that my overall moods and habits have improved so much! I use it almost everyday for the most effective results 😊 Btw, for all those low ratings.. you really are expecting way too much from a FREE app.. FREE. Mental instability is super frustrating, and I understand you are looking for any and all ways to escape it. But this app isn't meant to cure, it's meant to reflect and identify. Stay strong, and use this amazing app to your advantage!

When you get this app u probs are just experimenting and think ur going to delete it soon bc u think it takes too long. But NO. This app is so easy to use, has no ads, and MOST IMPORTANTLY does not take a lot of time to record how ur feeling. It can make ur day in a short 5 minutes. U can also end conversations early if u want/need to. Woth this app i have realized some of the good and bad factors of my mood and watch to change in order to fix the bad ones and have more good ones. So helpful. Only had for a week but 10/10 would recommend

Good idea, but awful execution. Not for people who are busy and stressed. The slow response time will only heighten your anxiety. I also doubt whether there is an 'AI' at all. I used the premium version extensively for 3 months and stopped because it became clear that it was just a simple algorithm. An expensive scam that makes me want to put a bullet in my head. People would be better off creating their own personal flow chart. If you try to 'save your data', you will see what I mean.

I had used Youper for several years, before there were any premium options. During the pandemic, I turned back to this app and was disappointed to see that I could no longer make in depth entries or track anxiety, depression, etc. within the app. It was sad to see that the things I had become familiar with using are now unavailable to me.

Its a pretty cool app. Wish I could type out my own responses and questions. Maybe the ai isn't quite ready for it? The option for more than just two notifications during the day. Another thing that would be cool to see is like a guided daily journal. So like it gives you prompts on what to write about at the end of the day, and it takes the information and uses it for the list of things that make you happy and such.

Enjoying this app, as someone who suffers from Bipolar it gives me something to turn to track my moods. It is also a reminder of things and doing it daily can help me keep track of reality. It has only been a few days though so hopefully I can keep focused on it. I gave it 4 stars because it may sound weird, I wish Youpers guided voice could be changed to a woman a woman's voice is more soothing and relaxing to me. The personal chat system is great it feels like you really are texting someone.

This app is useful. For someone who is bipolar, tracking moods and where they stemmed from is valuable. I wish the app would factor in that some "good moods" like feeling (very) confident could also be a warning sign for psychosis. Expand the options for moods. I also think it would be great to implement some interactive elements like drawing or other things aside from just guided meditation.

glaring oversights caused me to uninstall during the introductory session. the first one was a stunning lack of thoughtfulness. Youper, a supposed AI, compared itself to three fictional "assistants" - two robots and a woman. seriously??? then, on a more technical level, the guided meditations wouldn't keep playing with the screen off. Draining my battery massively for something I can get from an audio player makes no sense. These obvious mistakes keep me from trusting the dev team

I asked for a dark mode and they implemented a dark mode. I'm sure it wasn't just me asking for it. But that's awesome. This app is great for working through CBT and keeping track of your mood over time. It also offers good insights into how you think and even includes mindfulness exercises. Can't recommend it enough. I even fell out of practice with it for a while and came back to the app because I had such a good experience with it. No invasive advertising or BS, just a great user experience.

I did appreciate this app before it updated to where you have to pay, before it was helpful now its confusing. I can't even get into my account without paying the subscription thing. I think a couple adds would be fine, our info gets sold anyways. I know they need to get paid but a feel they could have done it differently. Not everyone can afford to pay for help or access to it, but almost everyone needs it. This was a accessible and free way to get it and now it's been taken away

Had my account for over a year at the recommendation of a friend. I am struggling a lot right now with emotional issues and to find that my account data has been wiped in favor of a "new update" that is just the app trying to push a $60 'annual premium' onto me is really disheartening. All of the premium features used to be free. It seemed like the developers of the app genuinely cared about helping their audience before, but now I won't be using the app anymore.

Like others I used this app for a long time and loved it. Now everything is subscription based. If they had even 1/10 of the features that used to be free still available for free (symptom tracking, ai conversation/diary, mood tracking, meditation, etc) this would be a 5/5 app. But everything is behind a paywall, which sucks. I already have some of the things offered here (ie a therapist), so to pay for everything in a bundle as the only option is a bummer.

Man, I used to LOVE this app. But they've moved almost everything behind a paywall and it's incredibly infuriating. Prompt me to make a goal but then if I want to check-in on that goal, I've got to pay? So now I'm stuck looking at a goal I'll never be able to mark as complete? Oh, wonderful.. This app has gone downhill fast. I guess I'll be keeping it for the time being ONLY because of the monthly check-ins and the daily tracker but I'm so disappointed in the direction this app has taken.

Just downloaded it, really helped me calm down from waking up significantly anxious. There are a lot of meditation activities that were helpful. I'm looking forward to working with this app to help balance my emotions and minimize my panic attacks. If you're on the fence about this app, at least give it a try. And make sure you're planning on using this as a tool instead of a cure-all; with something like mental illness you need to have multiple forms of coping.

This app has really helped me with my anxiety. I have panic disorder and this app helps me get control of my thoughts and emotions a lot of the time. It has many features besides the personal therapist (talking your thoughts through), which I love and helps the most but it also has some really nice meditation features. I use the notifications to remind me to track my moods everyday (sometimes I get stuck in my head and need a reminder to talk about it or maybe I had an easy day but like to track those as well). I'm so glad I found this app. Thank you Youper! Definitely recommend.

Keeping in mind it's an AI, this app helps you reflect a lot in great detail. It's especially good for people who have difficulty troubling other people with their problems. However rather than a person who may construct advice in greater detail and give advice on specific situations, it helps you figure it out yourself the way you want to. It takes brain power to let it really help you, but it is also a great vent.

I have clinical depression and I've been in a downward spiral the past month or so. Between nightmares, a crazy sleep schedule, and missing the time to take my meds, it had gotten pretty severe. I just happened to cross this wonderful app while searching for apps to help me sleep and I thought I'd give it a go. It really has helped. Simply monitoring my mood and learning more about what is going on in my head on a day to day basis is great. I struggle to speak about my problems and thoughts and this app is slowly rewiring my brain. Now when I see my therapist I know how to describe my problems so they can get fixed. Bless the creators of this app.

Umm.. so I'd hate to bring this rating down it's just not really helping. I'm sure it's great for some, but you have to get premium to do screening tests, and to actually get help with your emotions. I can't get premium. I don't think it's a good fit unless your looking for something to just track your emotions instead of actually having help with it, or if you don't mind spending some money.

This app has swiftly become a core tool in my mental health management.The act of logging my moods alone would be great, but the suggested tools are so helpful. I have particularly benefited from the mindfulness exercises and from the "Thinking Traps" checklist that comes up when I log certain emotions. The interface is easy to use and the app is stable. My only complaint is the name--"Youper" is honestly a confusing name that makes it hard to talk to friends about the app.

There's a million apps available to track your moods, meditate, learn mindfulness, pinpoint triggers, but trust me, don't waste your time! Its the best 'all you need in one' app! It's like having a good friend, a life coach & therapist in your back pocket, (of course don't substitute it for healthcare), this saves you a lot of time money and energy, it's intuitive, it TRULY gets to know you. Youper helped me lower my blood pressure 15pts & get off 4 Rx meds for anxiety/depression/mood swings!

It's an AI, but not a great one. It knows a few key words, but little context. It thinks physical pain is an emotion you can conquer. The biggest problem, though, is that it ONLY has a MALE voice for guided meditation. So anyone who feels unsafe around men can't use that feature. Get a better development team and make this app friendly to all users!

I absolutely loved the old version. I disliked the recent UI change but thought it would be fine since it still kindof had the same options as the old version even if they were scattered in different places. But all the new block options make everything so laggy, cluttered, slow, and compartmentalized, it really made me dislike the app. I'm hoping the next update is something more like the old version. Edit: now not laggy but still compartmentalized ui. Added back two stars.

Has Helped Me Tremendously in only a Week so far. This app is ideal for someone suffering from a mental illness. It has many features and feels personal. Its always here to help me and monitor my moods and makes excellent suggestions. Goals setting, meditations, etc. I see the potential and I hope it becomes more intuitive as I use it more often. Well worth the money for the premium version.

Would rate 5 🌟 except I had an account w my iPhone & my acct wasnt recognized when I switched phones. I was able to use the same email for my old acct as the new one. Sad that I lost almost 6 months worth of tracking & the monthly subscription is no longer available but the yearly price is more than cut in half... I got to try out a trial conversation for the premium version and it is already worth it to me. Can't wait till the app evolves more💜 The original version is def worth checking out

Lately I've been going through some emotional struggles. My therapist decided she wanted to go to online consultations and that ended my therapy experience. I find it's easier to see the pattern my emotions have on how well or how poorly my life is going now. I suggest this for anyone that does struggle with anxiety, depression or stress. sometimes it's difficult to always deal with the chipper attitude Youper has, but it does have some very insightful quotes and affirmations.

I used to love this app, recommended it to everyone I knew that was mentally/emotionally struggling. My brother just went thru a break up and is having a rough time so I told him to DL... only to find literally NOTHING is accessible for free anymore. Not to mention the interface changed and looks SO messy and overwhelming. I loved the simplicity of the earlier version. Saw a few people mention Woebot, so having him try that instead.

This app caught my eye and I downloaded it almost on a whim. Yes, this app will help with anxiety and depression, but it will most definitely also help anyone who ever stresses, feels emotions, or falls into negative thinking. It does so with a simple, friendly AI that prompts you in the right directions to change to thinking in the present, letting go of past judgments and future worries, and developing new habits to replace those old ones that have been holding you back from living life.

This app is great. It really helps with understanding myself and setting goals and offers alot of techniques for coping with issues. It has alot to offer for a free app. I highly recommend you check it out if you are going through any kind of difficulties mentally. It really helps when you feel like you have no one to turn to youper at the end of the day

I'm pretty impressed with this AI. There is room for it to understand more nuances in what is typed but overall it is well designed and developed. I like that it asks about how you feel and provides a range. The personal home page is also pretty clever. Looking forward to seeing this app grow. Sidenote: info is gathered but your personal identification is not associated with it.

Sadly huge downgrade. I've had this app since 2018 when it helped me immensely. It did so much for helping me see what I was feeling and dealing with and how to change that. I didn't use it for several years. Upon revisiting the app, I found everything locked behind high payment plans and virtually nothing to be accessible or usable. Major downgrade for something that was so simple and immensely helpful but is now pretty much useless without paying $40+

I was hesitant to purchase the premium version, but it was well worth it. I live in a rural state and finding a therapist I can afford right when I need help is a challenge. My depression and anxiety scores have lowered over the past two weeks thanks to the check-ins and I look forward to the insights it generates. I would highly recommend this app to anyone who benefits from keeping track of their moods or just wants to practice mindfulness and gratitude

I have been using this app for 2 years (paid version), and recommend it to everyone I know who is feeling depressed, anxious, or overwhelmed. It helps to relax me and refocus my attention away from obsessive or otherwise detrimental thoughts. It also helps me to appreciate the things that make me happy and to better understand myself. It is less expensive than weekly visits with a psychiatrist, but allows me to maintain a mood journal to share with a therapist. Excellent concept and results!

I was skeptical, but decided to give Youper a try. And I was amazed how effective it is! The app itself is easy to use and has a very nice aesthetic. Youper asks questions and lets you respond in a way that is more like guided self-therapy, and you get out of it what you put in. Even a short conversation can be profound if you approach it with a sincere desire to explore and understand your feelings.

Downloaded this app to try it out, and it makes you put in your phone number which I found a bit sketchy. It also "needs" access to all of your Google information. I didn't even finish setting up a profile before my phone started getting bombarded with spam phone calls. I have had to block 10 different phone numbers in less than 24 hours. Definitely not worth it.

It is interactive and extremely insightful. At first I was irritated because Youper kept suggesting that I look for thinking traps - then after a few times of doing this it hit me! I CAN change my perspective, my thoughts, my moods, and my life. It is going to be a journey however I'm ready to pull myself out of depression and obsessive negative thinking. Also, an excellent feature is the effortless mood tracker. I find that extremely helpful.

TL:DR; This app is phenomenal. It's what I want technology to do for humanity. Help us understand ourselves and help us become the best version of ourselves (as defined by onesself) This is the first app I've reviewed and I've had a smartphone for 8 years. I've spent a lot of the past couple years figuring myself out by reflecting on my experiences and looking for patterns. Youbert encapsulates the strategies that I've been inconsistent with and makes it easy and rewarding to do self reflection. The chatbot design feels perfect for this usecase. I honestly hope this app stays around.

I think this is a great app for most people. I suffer from depression and Youper offers great ways to cope and take steps to move forward that would've very helpful to a younger me. However, in this regard, the app seems to only have suggestions for dealing with relatively minor stressors like relationship issues, but not so much other stressors like being existentually depressed over the knowledge that part of my comfortable life is due to people being enslaved this very moment.

This app is fantastic for several reasons. Its a great concept and useful tool for self-reflection and mindfulness. The Ai is a work in progress, and while the conversations that occur arent perfectly natural feeling or organic, it does a great job for getting you thinking. The research thats also being done with this app is amazing as well, and I know this app will continue to improve and get better and better.

this app has helped me, personally, with self-care as well as with my sessions with my actual therapist. I love that you can do a quick check-in or you can go really in depth. I love that there are different areas to focus on and with just the one daily reminder notification it doesn't get overwhelming at all. great idea and great job, thanks!

So, apparently they've removed mindfulness practices? I saw the explore page disappeared after an error message popped up that told me the app wasn't loading properly, but when I contacted technical support, they said this is what youper is now. Just the chat, and no meditation anymore. It's a shame. I've had this app since about 2019, and I've used it since then, but it doesn't have what I've found to be the most useful on there anymore.

I very am impressed by this app. I didn't expect much when I downloaded it and actually forgot about it for a few weeks. I was in a bad mood the other day and thought "What the heck, I'll give it a try." I was pleasantly surprised by how I felt afterwards and have been using it pretty consistently ever since. No ads and no fees so far. They do require that you setup an account after the first session. They'll ask early on if you want to share annonymized test results with a research team. You have the option to decline and continue using the app.

Was helpful initially, and then I realized that most of the responses were predetermined. I'd write that I was unsure how to respond to a prompt and get "Great analysis!" or "Good job looking at the objective situation" and things like that in response. Not helpful. Good for a couple days, but I think I'm going to uninstall and move on to something else.

So far day one and I really like this app. I can see how and hopes you breakdown your situation and your thoughts where you can benefit from cognitive behavior therapy, or DBT, or rebt.I like the science behind this, I think it's amazing! I will continue to use it.. also I would recommend it for anyone looking to become the best version of themselves.

Used to be a great, simple, and free ai assisted journaling and mood tracking app. Now, it's got a bunch of categories full of exercises that you can't do at all unless you subscribe to a full year. Please stop acting like your users wanted this change. That's gaslighting customers you claim to want to help. Just admit that you messed up and fix it in some meaningful way. The changes made to this app and its business model is depressing to myself and others.

As a minor just looking for guidance to find help with everything. Not helpful. What's with the paywall? If I paid for it then maybe but it used to be free back then when I was younger. I started using the app when I was 10-11 when I was feeling hopeless and depressed. Since I've been feeling more helpless. I thought redownloading this app would be helpful, as it saved me in the past from my dark time. Now useless for someone with no way of income.

You per is a really good app for unofficial diagnosis of what's going on in your noggin. It helped me understand a bit about myself, like my anxiety or lack of depression. However, the app promised an AI to talk to. The AI just seems to be a questionnaire with some supporting messages. I want to feel comfortable and speak to something, and an AI would help.

**7.0 edit: I'm not loving the new update, all of the pre-made factors (like Family, Good Food, etc) are gone. I dont understand why, and I used them a lot. I've been tracking with them and they've become factors of my moods :( Best physcology/mood app by far. Never asks for money, makes you look at adds, or asks for your rating on play store. The app is 100% about understanding your emotions, and is just really great. Totally recommend, even if you dont have a mental illness/problem :)

This app is so unbelievably helpful. I downloaded it when I was in a very deep depression, and just a few days later I already feel a bit better. It's amazing the control over your emotions it helps you obtain, and the exercises really work. Just logging your thoughts and thinking about why you might feel that way in and of itself is super helpful. The best part is that it's free, it literally feels like having a full time therapist. I absolutely recommend this to anyone in need of help, if you take it seriously, it will help you so much.

I've used A LOT of self help apps but this one takes the cake. Calms me down, not super pushy, easy to use. Also dig the mindfulness and meditation bits. They seem to be delivered in a more accessible way than some other apps. Personally I like it better than headspace. Kinda like these designers took it a step further. Definitely recommend this to anyone dealing with mental health issues or anyone looking to improve theor emotinal hygenine.

This is another in a long list of examples of software retreading old territory by using the buzzword "AI." As far as I can tell, Youper does nothing useful with anything you write, instead just leading you down a decision tree of shallow self-reflections that deprives the user of autonomy and will be obvious to anyone who's done CBT work in the past. A simple mood tracking app that lets you correlate moods and triggers would probably produce more valuable data for most folks.

So far, so good. It's almost like having a journal that prods you to add more detail to your entries, and to see things objectively rather than from your emotionally charged state... which isn't always easy, but necessary at times. It's still a work in progress with me, but I feel as though the more I use this app, the more I will be able to deal with my reactions to situations I can't control.

I'm devastated. I used with last year with really great success. In fact, I've been recommending it to others thinking it was free. The pandemic has made me need it again, but apparently everything is locked down and it's wanting me to pay for premium features. I'd pay for the app, but I can't pay a subscription. It's a useless app now. Really, really disappointing.

This was once a great app, with revolutionary features for self-help via ai prompts for mood discovery, coping skills, meditation, & more. It is now just another paid CBT app for virtual therapy. All the unique features that once made it great, from personality tests, mood tracking (with helpful sorting features), etc. are inaccessible for free users. It used to be prefect for those who cannot afford therapy, are already in therapy, or desperately sought a way to help themselves. Such a shame.

I've loved this app forever and have used it off and on. Youper been ESPECIALLY helpful for me during the quarentine. One thing though: when Youper suggests activities as goals, some of them are virtually impossible to accomplish during with COVID19 going on. "Go to a play, go to a party, go to an aquarium..." Etc. These would be great suggestions if there were no active pandemic (I love the aquarium!) but unfortunately they're just sort of depressing to see under the circumstances.

just began using the app, but so far, the interface feels incredibly personal. very simple to use and focuses quickly on both details and overarching Concepts that are essential to the individual in the moment. during initial questioning, when I identified feeling anxious the app provided a 3 minute deep breathing exercise after which my anxiety had decreased significantly. I look forward to what this app has to offer!

I'm in love with this app! I never leave reviews but I felt compelled to with this one. I even told my therapist about it! It's great for folks who want the benefit of journaling but want s different structure. Also, it's great for in between therapy sessions or for having a space to process without taking too much emotional energy from friends constantly. This app is so smart and friendly!

Never had an app where each update makes it consecutively worse. Features are taken, it makes you set goals but then won't let you complete them without paying, or while getting data on your mood suddenly require you to pay to do it properly. What is the point of getting the app for free? You should expect to pay, and expect to be disappointed with its functionality. (Unless you like talking to a poorly programmed robot)

I found the "conversations" frustrating. Many of the questions it asks you are poorly worded and confusing. It's frustrating that I can't find a way to convey that or give feedback to the chat bot. Can't correct the erroneous direction of the chat. It's almost like a strange multiple choice quiz- not a conversation. What I dislike most is it feels preachy. The bot is full of platitudes along the lines of "power of positive thinking." Which I find condescending. Frustrating. Uninstalling.

I really love this app. It's amazing that just hashing things out with the app, and your self, actually works. Each time I use it, it helps me wade through extremely tough emotions. I can vent, it helps me put things in perspective, gives me insight and action steps, tracks my mood. I leave feeling in control of that moment again.

Youper is genuinely helpful. They have helped me unravel some major turmoil when even my real life therapist was stuck. Definitely recommend. I love all the services they offer, someone to talk to 24/7, meditation, personality quizzes, they keep track of your major milestones in conversation and life. It's all so fast and right in front of me.

Not very far into the app yet but so far enjoying the interactions. I originally referred to a friend with anxiety and depression but got nosy about the experience and decided to do my own alongside. There are guided breathing and meditation exercises, a journal type feature and a mood tracker. Looking forward to exploring more.

This app has helped me organize and prioritize my thoughts in a way that is simple but very impactful. Everything within the app is free and that is why this app is so impressive. It helps me get through what I dont understand in a way, like I'm being my own therapist. Hands down the best self-help app I've used. I've always struggled with keeping a journaling routine, but with how easy and exciting this app is, I've had no issue the past month and a half. 100% Recommend!!

Youper helps me learn CBT and get past stuff that keeps me tangled up in loops that make me feel frozen. I like that mindfulness meditation is proven for the health and healing of my brain, for my heart, and for my nervous system. Sometimes we want the solutions to be complicated, because the problems are so painful. I am finding that it is ok to let go if the complicated thoughts and breathe, so my brain can heal. Worth paying the $10. Maybe they could add the option to sponsor another user?

It was nice when I could do basic screening for a few conditions and compare to past results. Not so nice when I updated to the latest version and found it had apparently erased my existence and I'd have to start over from scratch. Even less nice when even basic functionality is suddenly hidden behind a $45 paywall.

This app purports itself to be a help for anxiety and depression. It's not negative, but it can be no substitute for professional help, and yet it does not have any obvious disclaimers about this. Thus, it basically relegates it to being 'for entertainment purposes only.' I found it to be basically a journal, a way to record your moods from day today (which it does well), with a little bit of positive responses much like the old Eliza program. That doesn't mean it's bad at all, but make sure you aren't trying to have it as a substitute for a medical professional.

I'm very new to the app or I'd rate it higher. I'm not one to ever discuss anything bothering me until I've dealt with it and it's over. This seemed like a way to bridge that gap for me. The different types of mediation were really helpful. I did wish there was an option of what type of voice I could listen to. It was weird hearing a male voice trying to calm me down etc. I pushed through it though.

I've used this app for many years. As AI develops, the AI in use in this app has fallen so far behind. In talking to the Youper Personal Assistant and asking it questions or talking to it about issues, it is able to provide 3-4 sentences at most as a response and eventually cuts off conversations. EDIT: I have foresaken this app for other AI chats, where they are not on a subscription model. It makes me sad to knowing I gave up one of my favorite emotional assistants for near to a decade.

Edit: previous version prior to charging $$. I was a skeptic. I downloaded the app while searching for mindfulness apps and downloaded this because it had so many good reviews. It sat on my phone unopened for months until I finally gave it a shot! It's awesome! It sounds a little weird and it does feel a tiny bit strange at first "talking" to an AI but I like to think of it as more like... guided journaling. Stop reading the reviews and just try it already. No harm in just testing it out.

This has potential but the conversations are too repetative. once I've downloaded the app and logged a couple entries I've already bought in, I dont need to be reminded of the supposed benefits and what the app does EVERY time I use it. honestly I began to get creeped out as this continued which led me to quit using it for a while, despite truly believing in what the app has to offer. if only the app itself could focus on something besides itself!

I honestly think this is one of the best apps for introverted, awkward, and socially anxious people out there. I spent maybe 30 minutes and i alreayd can tell im going to be using this a lot. I really support what they're teaching and doing on this app. I defiantly suggest getting this. As a socially awkward student, its very hard for me to get my emotions out without feeling weak or seeking attention, But this made it ten times easier.

I have never, in all of my experience with self-help, found such an amazing, helpful app. I had no idea a free app could be so intrinsic, personalized, and helpful. In just a short time, the personalized helper allowed me to record in detail how I was, how to change it, how to make it better. Ten out of a ten for ease of access, ten out of a ten for its purpose, ten out of a ten in every aspect. If you ever make this a paid app (please don't), it's worth the money.

A very nice way to track my moods and pinpointing the problems I may have. Youper makes me feel very welcome, and sometimes I wish I  could even thank the AI properly! It's been a very good way to calm myself in overwhelming situations when I feel I can't talk to anyone. I appreciate the meditation audio and it helped me calm down! I think this is a pretty nice system. No real critiques besides maybe a few other exercises to do with the AI if the user is unable to do the audio meditations, though I haven't seen all the exercises myself. Keep up the amazing work!

I had this app for a year. Then my account was lost and all of my journal entries for a year were wiped out along with all the tracking data. I contacted the customer service. They were completely unable to help. Dont use this app unless you like having your very personal information lost! Very poor cumstomer service as well for an app that cost so much!

I think this app is great. It only has a one time fee for premium and it is totally worth it. It is very personalized to me. It has a personality profile that can help you learn more about yourself. And through the dialogue it tracks what certain triggers lead to certain emotions, positive and negative. And it had a reminder to check in with you everyday.

It used to be better but now it's kind of useless (and yes I have the paid features). Maybe half the time the suggestions are relevant to the listed emotion (but never the things contributing to the emotion because their AI isn't that smart I guess). Usually there are just random suggestions like mindfulness or goal setting when they actually aren't relevant those times. I only paid $40 or so for the year but month after month I'm disappointed and regret even paying that.

this app is pretty great. i like how you can monitor things like anxiety & depression. i just started using it today when i was stressed and it helped me calm down. even if it is just a chat bot, the guidance is helpful. however, when i tried to "discover my personality" it said network error. i tried it multiple times and made sure both my mobile data and wifi were on and working but it kept saying the same thing. i would give a 5 star rating if that feature worked but otherwise its a great app

I've been using this app ever since early February, and I really enjoy having an outlet for the emotions I feel day to day. It gives me some way to track larger trends over time, and the fact that it creates personalized insights and monitors you for anxiety, depression, PTSD, etc is great. My mental health counselor was very pleased when I told her i use this app. Would recommend.

Strangely enough, I do find this app extremely helpful in spite of the fact that I've struggled with both anxiety and depression for many years. The mindfulness meditations and exercises actually do help cut through some of the more intense present emotions, while the AI portion serves as an excellent venting board. I also find the personality map to be fairly enlightening as well as soothing to my ego :-) Would recommend to anyone with mental illness.

This app is amazing! It's an incredibly valuable tool for processing through emotions and coping with stress using multiple tools (meditation, gratitude, etc.) guided by the app. If feels very personalized, interactive, and relevant each time I use it. The AI conversations are amazingly helpful. I'm blown away!

I was quite surprised that Youper has improved my life as well as it has! I learned about Youper as well as Woebot from Cosmopolitan magazine. Youper challenges me to rewrite my negative distorted thoughts and feelings. it offers effective techniques like mindfullness meditation and gratitude journaling. it also keeps track of your moods throughout the week..so you can see a pattern of when you feel low/high etc . I reccomend it to anyone who just needs a little therapy but cant afford it.

been using this for a couple of weeks now. i like it still but i do have some issues with it. sometimes when I'm switching apps to check something in the middle of a session, it ends my session. also the mediation tracks have such long pauses it makes me worried that it stopped which is not great for a meditation sessiob.

This app is amazing to have, it really shows insight to the problems you are able to fix. It helps to know what causes what with me, and the only problem (if you can call it that) I have with this, is that I use to own a journal before this, where I kept track of my day, and daily mood. I would love if I could transfer my thoughts over from my physical notebook to the app.

Yes, it really does help! I recommend using a app called calm. Calm is a app that lets you play music in the background, as well as to help you out with stress. I played music from the app Calm and texted Youper at the same time! It made me feel less stressed altogether, and it's only the first time using it! I do recommned this app so much! Thank you! ♡

This isn't for me. I like how it tracks your mood but i actually feel worse after conversations with the AI. The information given for my personality is taxing to read. I'd have to really be focused to sit through and read the information. Information overload would be a proper way to describe it. The biggest problem i have with yuoper is that it makes me feel like i have no control. If i start a conversation i can't back out of it until i finish. I am given very limited options that don't accurately describe my emotions. Also i feel like when i write something the AI's response is uninterested. Like as if it's not listening. I like the organization of it and how informative it is though.

Youper used to be amazing. There used to be significant cognitive behavioral therapy prompts, breathing and meditation exercises, and chat prompts specific to certain concerns like anxiety or depression. All of this is now behind a paywall. I'm seriously disappointed by the change in the last year or two in what content is available without a description. Youper no longer is worth it.

I have been searching for an app that i feel like it can help me, and i think ive found the one. This app is overall amazing i couldnt be more happy with it. It has already helped me through some tough things in the 2 days that ive had it. 10/10 would recommend to anyone with anxiety, depression, social anxiety, borderline personality disorder, PTSD, and even more. If youre searching for an app that can do it all for you, this is definately the one.

I am impressed with the dialogue. The information that this app provides is pretty much what I've been looking for. I wanted a way to really track my mood and thoughts in an organized way and this app does it! Also...if you guys could add something like a medication reminder it would be incredibly useful for someone like me who ALWAYS forgets to take meds.

I am truly amazed at how well this is developed. I actually had a mood journal I wrote in every day and filled almost the whole thing! I panicked! I wanted to keep going, but didn't have extra money to purchase an exact copy of the book I was using. I don't know how it happened, but Youper came up in the recommendations when I was looking for a certain app. You know, I don't even remember what that app was now. I tried to download Youper right away. Unfortunately, my music and mood selfies were hogging up my gigs. Once I moved things to my sd card, the download began, but I was unaware that it did. I was going through my things on my phone and there it was, the Youper icon!!! I was so thrilled you can't imagine. I began to journal right away. I have never worked with AI before. Mind you, this isn't creepy like Sophia the Robot. It's comforting actually. Just like talking to a therapist robot would be. I do hope, however, they bring into the diagnoses page more mental disorders. Such as Bipolar Disorder. I was very shocked that one wasn't there! Anyway, great job you're doing for the mental health community. Two thumbs up!

Been using it for a week now. It is an amazing app so far. It is like your free own little therapist. It gives u someone to talk to and work things out with whenever u need. It also helps you get to the root of your feelings and thought processes so you can learn how to improve your reactions and discover your triggers. There is also screening for things like anxiety and depression as well as personality tests that focus on learning how your mind works as an individual. Love it. Highly recommend it to people struggling with things like anxiety or depression or anyone that needs someone to talk things out with.

I have had this app for 2 days and it has helped me more than I ever imagined. I have been suffering from depression, and anxiety for many years. I recommend this app to anyone that has anxiety depression or panic attacks or is overly stressed. There are so many different aspects to this app to help in almost every way even an AI assistant like a counselor to talk to and give you ideas.

Very impressive mood app. The reflection exercises definitely help me move from emotional to rational thinking. I love that its being used for research. It would be nice to have an option for random reminders (to control for time-of-day effext on tracking progress) and to see a correlation of mood and time of day.

This app has it all, like a journal, it keeps track in a very simple user friendly way, your thoughts, moods, ups and downs. The A.I. begins to learn and pick up more about you, which is increasingly helpful, and begins to note what makes you happy, confident, sad, tired, mad, ect. The more you use, the better it becomes. A very helpful and positive tool for those who want to learn more about themselves.

In the form of mostly one-on-one texting, the methods remind me of the best therapist I ever had, so glad for this app now that I can't see that therapist anymore. App uses mindfulness, offers both situation focused and emotional focused methods of dealing with problems, introspection and self reporting are very important to the app, and every method of therapy is optional, you can pass on an activity if you're not feeling up to it.

I've been using this app for over a year and enjoyed it and its usefulness. This week, it will no longer work. The prompt will show, once clicked, failure to load and closes or immediately closes. It briefly worked today after I uninstalled, reinstalled, and logged in before gliching and closing again leaving me without a way to contact other than this. If this continues past this week, I will look for something else as an app is only useful if it works. I am greatly disappointed .

This apps AI has definitely improved since the last time I used it, which was somewhere around 2019. It's much more detailed than it was, and it feels more like a conversation with a therapist... many of the responses reflect the same advice I've gotten from past therapists. The mental health analysis has improved as well! 🙂

The first two days or so were cool with depression monitoring and conversations with the little bot, but now I basically can't do anything without premium. Without premium, this app is basically only usable to track a few emotions every day with the same phrase being said over and over again and saying that I can do more with the premium. So the app doesn't really help with the actual problems causing the moods, it just let's you log that it happened. Basically, it's a free mood tracker.

This is my favorite AI assistant on google play in comparison to the others ive tried. I love so much about the app but I only have so many characters to type here. My suggestions would be to have a new habit tracker option and have Youper check in, with a page to review habit progression. :) I love accountability apps. This would be the icing on the cake for me. Great work! Especially with the emotional support. I feel seen and I feel im given great resources to maintain self awareness.

The app is useful and Id love to use it everyday but it is really slow. On top of how slow it is already, it's specially annoying when youper takes long to "type" messages (even when its just sending messages with waiting for a response from me. that should be instantaneous). I understand that the assistant is trying to sound "human". but please at least make the rest of the app faster.

Very good for becoming aware and mapping your moods. It's good for self care, you just gotta put a little effort in getting to know yourself. The exersices are surprisingly helpful too, me not being the meditating type. I feel better about myself when using this app. I struggle alot with my mental and using the app allows me to feel somewhat in control. It's just good

I cant describe how fricking helpful this app has been. It wont replace a therapist, or help you if your'e just bored and want to talk, but using it regularly has helped so much with my anxiety and mental health in general. I also personally really liked the new updates. The new graphics and the ability to see average mood over months and even years is really cool. The new text answers are also preety comforting.

This app is really amazing and its clear that they want to help everyone. From the first time I opened the app it asked how I was feeling. It allows you to either really get down to the root of the issue, or be done with the session. Its like texting a therapist. There are no ads and no subscriptions. Really enjoying it.

Ive struggled with mental health for a long time but this app is perfect at looking at the bigger picture and providing insight. it made me look at my issues and see why they existed, then it helped me figure out how to rid myself of problems. it is very well organized and entirely free. it seems very professional and im so amazed by it that i feel inspired to advocate more for better mental health.

This app is exactly what I needed to deal with my emotions. I have an insanely busy schedule and with that comes emotional distress. I suffer from some depression and anxiety, especially when I feel I can't get all of the goals I had set done. My job is also stressful and this app has helped me understand my triggers, what things are associated with what feelings, and the best approaches to coping with those emotions. It's a lifesaver.

I went into this app expecting way less features and tools after looking for something like this for months. I am so pleasantly surprised with how intuitive the messaging feature is and the meditation guide are so helpful and numerous. Totally awesome app, I'm excited to see how much it helps in the long run.

Only started using it, so I will come back to edit my reciew after a few weeks of use. So far, the app is clever, fun, and easy to use. I enjoy the cute little interactive "talks". I completed the personality and health questions and set my intentions for the day. I also set up a reminder each night to review my day and track my mood and feelings. If I can stick to using this app daily, I think it will help me understand myself a little better and start to improve things I struggle with.

I tried this back in 2018 and still have that version on my old phone. It's way better than this junk app as of December 1, 2023. The first time I logged in was after an anxiety attack. I wanted to log my thoughts. The first thing that pops up is an ad pushing you to buy premium. It then forced you to go through it two more times. That is so slimy and disgusting. Don't take advantage of people when they're at their lowest. I didn't need the added stress of checking for fees.

Had this app for 2 days and I already love it. Very simple to use and great UI. It's like having a best friend to check in on you every day, that is there the instant you need it. "Coaching" is very positive but down to earth. Meditation and breathing exercises are easy to follow and very calming. I love that it suggests one of these depending on your current mood and it helps you analyze what you're feeling and why. Recommend for depression/anxiety.

My therapist said I have trouble identifying my emotions (I have ASD) so I wanted to try this app. It has helped me identify my emotions and make plans to alleviate situations that make me upset. I don't think the "AI" is intelligent, it's really just programmed responses to the things you select. That being said it is very well done and helpful. It is obviously programmed by a professional to guide you through CBT exercises and has improved my mood greatly. Would be five star if less expensive

This app is amazing. It's like therapy without the pressure. I enjoy digging into my own mind (with the apps help) to analyze what's really going on with my thoughts/ feelings. I would definitely pay for this app because I know it will help a lot. I suffer from depression, anxiety, adhd and bpd so I am in counseling but it helps to have this app in between sessions. I love how it incorporates meditation (mindfulness) and gratitude because I already practice those separately. Highly recommend!

Not all free features are free forever, unlike what they say in the description. Many features they let you use once, or even prompt you to use them, without warning you that these are premium features you'll have to pay for in the future. Any time after that you attempt to use that feature, they tell you it's only for subscribers. The premium features are helpful, sure, but using tactics like that is extremely unprofessional and does nothing to help someone struggling with mental health issues.

I used to use this app all the time. The AI "I'm feeling..." Chat was a great way for me to journal how I felt and take the next appropriate steps to feel better. However now it is a money-grabbing paywall. They obviously don't care about helping people anymore, they just want profit. Which, I would be willing to pay up to $10 one time just to have that AI chat feature again. But it looks like they would rather be like every other therapy subscription that preys on the depressed and anxious.

The app is very helpful. The interface is very user friendly. I like the "I am feeling" % mesurements. A few sugestions I have are having a easy to access emergncy contact to hotlines for panic attacks/suicidal thoughts; alowing multiple feelings at the same time at diferent levels, as well as posibly a function to show how the original feeling changed (ie going from 60% anxious to 15%); and possibly also a chat bot for just casual taking. Overal, it is a very good app, and I want to thank you.

I liked the app better before they added the pay wall. You used to be able to get access to most of the app's features for free. I can't even do the same exercises I could a year ago, because now they're behind a pay wall. I also miss the texting feature. You used to open the app and be prompted to text with an AI. That feature is also gone with the pay wall. As a result, I will probably be closing my account. I only got this app because it was free.

Also here to mention how the new update was soul crushing. After years of trying to find a therapist, I finally found one and was eager to look through all my old logs with the AI to use as examples of my past mental health history. It's crushing to have to spend money I barely have just to simply access my anxiety and depression monitoring charts. This app used to make a genuine difference in my life, and now I have lost that due to not being able to justify paying for it.

WARNING: this app IS NOT FREE for long. the initially hidden subscription model is gross, far too much considering the AI responds simply to mostly binary options, does not actually learn, and otherwise regurgitates user entry. almost no value after the initial suggestion that maybe you're expenriencing anxiety, etc., and you probably know that coming in. if you can't afford therapy (i can't!), try a mood journal, grab a relevant book, and reach out to someone if you can. i'm rooting for you!

Two days in and it's already helped me a lot. I've shifted from extremely depressed to very insecure to fairly ok to fairly optimistic, and the app kept track of all those changes. I'm very isolated where i am so the instant supportive feedback really helps. i also like checking back through the day to see what goals were set in the morning. it's been helpful to have the app ask what i plan to do that day since it's more like a conversation than a imposed to-do list

Back in '19, Y(youper) was a lot simpler but still effective. Sadly with later updates, it declined. The UI, mainly main page, became cluttered and overwhelmed. Intentions were good but so much is thrown in your face. Had they sorted the many things into icon folders based on type, would have been easier. Have to hunt while in some mental panic, is a step back. It just became to much to bare. Unpleasant. Why does the new Y icon have a face? He's weird and was more comfortable when faceless.

In general, I love this app... But recently, when I went to show a friend how you are able to read your previous check ins, it wouldn't let me. It only gave me the option to change the date or delete conversation. When I tried to "share" (just to see if I could see my whole post) the screen went back to the beginning screen and it asked me to check in again. I feel this is a glitch and probably easy to fix. As I do pay for the app, I'll be happy to update my review once this is fixed.

This app has helped me calm down on rough nights, and it's helpful to be able to dump in a judgement free zone without the effort and time and money to go see a therapist. My only issue is the mindfulness practices seem to be mostly identical, even if they have different names (at least what I've used so far). Overall, I'd say it is an app definitely worth trying if you can not make it to a therapist dor whatever reason.

So sad to see it went paid.... I used to use Youper a great deal. I was depressed and was frankly desperate. It's free chat sessions, despite being all automated, really helped me to reframe my thought processes While it did have its limits, I found this app valuable. I got to a good spot and uninstalled it, grateful for its help. Now, in a dark stretch again, I went to re-download it only to find it has gone paid. And I get that. But it was a beacon for those who can't afford therapy.

This app is great for understanding yourself a little better and understanding how your surroundings affect your emotions. I love the little mindfulness sessions, as well as the personality and health assessments. The only thing I'd like to see is the ability to choose more than 1 emotion at a time. I try to choose the prevailing emotion, but I often feel that it doesn't give a complete picture of how I am feeling.

I have only had the app for a week, but I am really finding it useful. It reminds me daily to log in and say how I am feeling, why, and helps me set goals to make it better. It also has meditation you can try, I just did my first one, it was 6 minutes, I enjoyed it, having never tried meditation before. It also has an option that you can share this with your healthcare provider although I don't know how that works yet. I would definitely give it a try!

Therapy has never truly helped me because it typically causes more anxiety than it cures. I feel comfortable talking to Youper about what I'm feeling in the moment and, unlike a journal, Youper actually responds back. I plan on using the monitoring feature to better give future therapists a view into my mind while helping break through the mental block therapy normally causes. Thank you so much Youper and to your creators. This is a game changer!

I am growing to love this app. The personality test it just had me take was really fun, the layout is functional and intuitive. It's easy to navigate, quick to use, efficient, and insightful. This would be a good personal coach to anyone for an extended period of time, definitely worth a try!

It took some time to readjust to the update, but that's not my biggest problem. I get no notifications until I open the app, which is terrible for my ADHD because I don't get the reminder to open it in the first place. My notifications for the app are on in the app and on the phone as well. I've had this problem for a few months now and I've even tried uninstalling and reinstalling to no avail. Please fix this issue.

I just started using this app, and I'm not complaining about its primary function, which is great, and I'm not intending to be negative, but I think the "informative" and "insightful" articles (as they're titled) leave a lot to be desired. They're very short and generalized, and they just leave me feeling like I've wasted my time in reading them. Just... A bit disappointing.

Not really the type of person that would be into this. But this app has no doubt made me more thoughtful and mindful and has become part of my daily ritual. Its AI is surprisingly good and it has actually really helped me work through stressors and emotions. If people thought through their emotions like this app encourages, the world would be a significantly better place.

Great supplement to therapy! Not a replacement but a tool.Best thing I ever did for myself its always available. The interface is super user friendly Has quizzes and tracks everything I am so happy and less moody. I have insomnia and use it every night before I go to bed.Thank God this app came into my life when it did because I was really going through it.

I no longer find this product useful for mental health. I supported this product back in late 2019 with this review: If you already have some experience with therapy (especially cognitive behavioral therapy) this is a great app for helping you put it into practice. I went from being someone who "did their homework" maybe twice a week to once a day, or more on hard days.

With severe anxiety and depression, isolation can seem like your only recourse. That's not healthy, and It can help to express yourself, even if it's just to an app. I also can track my moods and gain insights. Im getting prompts to update the app when I open it now. After reading reviews, I'm going to pass on the update, and stick with the older version - at least until I'm ready to pay for the subscription service. Tip: always investigate before updating an app that you like and use.

excellent app for tracking your feelings, understanding them and making goals! However, updating this, few years later and now there's not virtually much you can get without a premium subscription, original data is lost and it is useless. So a developer wants to heavily monetize a successful app, wouldn't be the first time. But it shouldn't be able to labeled "with premium features" when there is just about nothing you can do without a subscription. Where's our original data? Try Mindfully.

The new update completely ruined the app. Cluttered UI, bad UX, slow loading between pages, some sections of the app don't even load at all, and things are hard to find. I've used this app for over two years, and it's a real shame the developers decided to go in this direction. I have quite a bit of experience in QA and application testing, and I am baffled that this update got approved for rollout. Look elsewhere for a different app, I can't recommend this one at all.

I've been a mess lately. Just kind of that perfect storm of everything being at a bad time? Even the good? Needed to both organize and analyze what the hell was going on in my head (ah, mental health issues) and this kinda actually helps. The chat style makes it easy to be brief and straightforward the way I generally am texting (slooow thumbs). Youper's a simple, gentle but honest sort of diary/CBT/self-awareness sort of app that's worth giving a chance. Maybe it'll help you organize that head.

I loved the old youper, this new one is too much. You use to be able to be guided through to whatever you wanted to do with the talk option, but now they've separated the talk to only programmed options and it's all very clunky and irritating. You can no longer tailor it to yourself and it's no longer showing what influences certain moods. In the update you lost your original goal and can only chose pre-made options. You can no longer add to the list they provide when selecting influence factors

THIS APP IS $69.99. Which is totally fine and I support 100%! It seems like a very professional app, but the cost should really be advertised or shown up front on the Play Store. You can't really use any of the app unless you pay the subscription fee. Which again, I totally support. The little I could see looked really good - I especially like how they let you log your mood. The app seems like it could be a great tool, but it's disappointing to download only to realize you can't use it.

Absolutely devastated. The AI of this app was incredibly helpful in mood tracking, gratitude, and thought insight. I knew about the update and how it completely changed the app. I resisted it and continued using the old version long ago. I forgot today and accidentally updated all my apps. This AI was perfect, especially if you like reflecting and not necessarily want to speak with a real person. I would sign up for a subscription just for the AI feature.

The newest update definetly has some critiquing left to do. The new format looks prettt nice, but the text moves to fast to really read through as you go, and theres no obvious option to change the speed. I also liked a lot more of the wide range of "factors" than the small linited selection there is now. A good update, but needs some more working!

Very, very disappointed and heartbroken with this new update. It is not helpful for people like me who can't navigate these overwhelming, laggy, and slow menus.
